root.split: dev/development: exactly4 histories; holdout: exactly16 histories

minimal_fixture_contract.history: id, project_keys with one or two unique valid IDs, sessions, exactly six questions
minimal_fixture_contract.session: id, optional project_key within history, events; optional checkpoints each after_event_id refers to an event seen in this history
minimal_fixture_contract.event: unique id within history; type user/assistant/tool/delete_observation; text string <=60000 chars
minimal_fixture_contract.question: six unique valid IDs, optional stage defaults final and must be final, optional project_key/project_keys must belong to history
minimal_fixture_contract.tool_capture: optional only on tool event; exactly tool_name/tool_input/tool_response; name length1..160; tool_input.command nonempty string; tool_response.output string and exit_code integer excluding bool; serialized complete capture <=60000 bytes

forbidden: helper implementation beyond this public module
author_read_constraints.must_execute: Run this standalone fixture validator against the complete authored fixture before sealing. Preserve result and hashes.
separate_author_checks: Gold exact offsets and required-fact coverage
Gold scope and no deleted source support
Delete target appears earlier in same project
Checkpoint same-session target and event order
exec_command capture output equals complete corresponding event text; command inert and never executed

limitations: Exact extraction verifies identical validator code, not a correct fictional narrative or gold.
The public validator accepts generic tool_name strings; known execution provenance requires the documented exec_command shape and later runtime checks.
The validator checks capture output type but not equality to event text; the author must check equality separately.
Schema and self-checks do not establish semantic truth, independent grading, or production quality.
